overview: Per-spring source-water concentrations of chloride, arsenic and boron for the Midway Geyser Basin plus a Firehole upstream boundary value derived from the gauge chloride-conductance fit. Each value carries a status label and source metadata; some cited literature is only partially verified. Features without a verified published analytical row carry status authored_no_verified_sample.

sources.citation: Ball, J.W., McCleskey, R.B., and Nordstrom, D.K., 2010, Water-chemistry data for selected springs, geysers, and streams in Yellowstone National Park, Wyoming, 2006-2008: U.S. Geological Survey Open-File Report 2010-1192, 109 p.

McCleskey, R.B., Clor, L.E., Lowenstern, J.B., Evans, W.C., Nordstrom, D.K., Heasler, H.P., and Huebner, M.A., 2012, Solute and geothermal flux monitoring using electrical conductivity in the Madison, Firehole, and Gibbon rivers, Yellowstone National Park: Applied Geochemistry, v. 27, no. 12, p. 2370-2381, doi:10.1016/j.apgeochem.2012.07.019.
sources.verification_note: DOI resolves and metadata confirmed via search; the paper is behind an Elsevier paywall and was not fetched in full. The companion dataset (Clor et al. 2012 Data Series 632) was fetched and read in full.

sources.citation: Clor, L.E., McCleskey, R.B., Huebner, M.A., Lowenstern, J.B., Heasler, H.P., Mahony, D.L., Moloney, T., and Evans, W.C., 2012, Water chemistry and electrical conductivity database for rivers in Yellowstone National Park, Wyoming: U.S. Geological Survey Data Series 632, 18 p. plus data tables, available at http://pubs.usgs.gov/ds/632/.
sources.note: DS632 names gauges 06036805 (Firehole River above Old Faithful) and 06036905 (Firehole River near West Yellowstone MT) and the Aqua TROLL deployments; Lone Star Geyser is the only substantial thermal source upstream of 06036805.

sources.citation: Nimick, D.A., Moore, J.N., Dalby, C.E., and Savka, M.W., 1998, The fate of geothermal arsenic in the Madison and Missouri Rivers, Montana and Wyoming: Water Resources Research, v. 34, no. 11, p. 3051-3067, doi:10.1029/98WR01704.
sources.verification_note: DOI resolution was recorded; the full text has not been reviewed.

sources.citation: Water Quality Portal (National Water Quality Monitoring Council), discrete water-quality samples at USGS stations 06036805 and 06036905, accessed 2026-10-13.

chloride_mg_l.note: Pool water sample at Excelsior Geyser Crater; field pH 7.68, laboratory pH 8.59, field specific conductance 1663 uS/cm.

arsenic_ug_l.note: Arsenic (total) reported as 1.87 mg per L; stored here in ug per L.

chloride_mg_l.reason: Grand Prismatic Spring is not among the Midway Geyser Basin samples in Open-File Report 2010-1192 Table 11 (Excelsior Geyser Crater and unnamed Rabbit Creek drainages). Earlier Ball-McCleskey-Nordstrom Open-File Reports may carry a Grand Prismatic sample; those were not fetched in this session. Value is left unknown rather than invented.
Opal Pool is not among the Midway samples in Open-File Report 2010-1192 Table 11. Not fetched in this session.
Turquoise Pool is not among the Midway samples in Open-File Report 2010-1192 Table 11. Not fetched in this session.

firehole_upstream_boundary.feature_name: Firehole River above Midway Geyser Basin
firehole_upstream_boundary.chemistry_type: pre-Midway river water carrying Upper Geyser Basin discharge

chloride_mg_l.reason: Mean of the daily chloride series obtained by applying the 06036905 WQP paired-sample ordinary-least-squares fit to the 06036805 daily specific-conductance series over 2010-05-13 to 2017-10-30. The fit is in derived/firehole_chloride_sc_fit.json. 06036805 is downstream of Lone Star Geyser (the only substantial thermal source upstream per USGS Data Series 632) and upstream of the Upper Geyser Basin, so this value is a lower bound for the Firehole after the Upper Basin and before Midway.

arsenic_ug_l.reason: No arsenic samples at 06036805 in the Water Quality Portal query performed in this session; no published Firehole-above-Midway arsenic concentration was retrieved.

boron_mg_l.reason: No boron samples at 06036805 in the Water Quality Portal query performed in this session; no published Firehole-above-Midway boron concentration was retrieved.

excelsior_aggregate_outflow.note: The aggregate thermal outflow at the Firehole river entry carries the composition of the Excelsior pool. River-entry mixing with mats and cooling means the delivered concentration is an upper bound. Discharge is read from the replay lateral source and is never set in this data file.

chloride_specific_conductance_relation.reason: Fit on 19 WQP paired chloride and specific conductance samples at USGS 06036905 spanning 1984-02-28 to 2019-09-25. Slope and intercept are site-specific. McCleskey et al. 2012 reports site-specific chloride-conductance relations for Yellowstone thermal reaches but the specific slope and intercept per Firehole site were not read from the paywalled Applied Geochemistry article; comparison is reserved for a verification pass once the paper is accessible.

chloride_mg_l.reason: US EPA National Recommended Water Quality Criteria for Aquatic Life, chloride (freshwater), criterion continuous concentration 230 mg per L and criterion maximum concentration 860 mg per L.

sources.citation: US Environmental Protection Agency, National Recommended Water Quality Criteria - Aquatic Life Criteria Table, chloride CCC 230 mg per L, CMC 860 mg per L.

arsenic_ug_l.reason: US EPA National Recommended Water Quality Criteria for Aquatic Life, arsenic (trivalent), CCC 150 ug per L and CMC 340 ug per L.

sources.citation: US Environmental Protection Agency, National Recommended Water Quality Criteria - Aquatic Life Criteria Table, arsenic III freshwater CCC 150 ug per L, CMC 340 ug per L.

boron_mg_l.reason: Published salmonid boron effect thresholds vary; a no-effect-to-effect transition near 1 to 10 mg per L boron is reported for freshwater fish including salmonids by Eisler 1990 and summarized in CCME 2009; the Firehole Midway values can approach the low end of this range.

sources.citation: Eisler, R., 1990, Boron hazards to fish, wildlife, and invertebrates: a synoptic review: U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service Biological Report 85 (1.20), 32 p.
Canadian Council of Ministers of the Environment, 2009, Canadian water quality guidelines for the protection of aquatic life: Boron.

goldstein_2001.reference: Goldstein, J., 2001, Firehole River salmonid distribution; bibliographic detail requires verification.
goldstein_2001.note: Goldstein reports trout absence at the hottest geothermally influenced Firehole sites. The field study does not isolate thermal, arsenic and boron effects; the three stressors are candidate co-causes.

firehole_thermal_output_trend.finding: USGS reporting of the Firehole thermal-water output describes a decrease of about 10 percent from 1983 to 2011.
